title: Generated self-contained query runner for a Snowsight Workspace
scope: Two new files under rai_code/manual/ plus this report. Nothing under rai_code/aviation_model/, rai_code/queries/, rai_code/notebooks/, data/ or EXPECTED_ANSWERS.yaml was modified, no test suite was re-run, and no data was changed. One throwaway Snowflake notebook object, PK_AVIATION_TEMPORAL.NOTEBOOKS.RUNNER_SMOKE, was created purely to execute the runner server-side; it is not part of the demo.
requirement: One self-contained .py file that runs every question in both use cases plus the rotation, prints question, parameters, row count, elapsed time and result rows, and executes both locally and inside a Snowsight Workspace.

design.generated_not_hand_written: run_all_queries.py is emitted by _gen_run_all_queries.py, following the _gen_standalone.py precedent. The generator copies no query logic. It embeds aviation_model._gen_standalone.render() (the live ontology, not the checked-in artifact) and the byte-for-byte text of rai_code/queries/{uc1,uc2,rotation}.py, then dispatches through the tables those modules already publish.

dispatch.Q01,Q02,Q02F,Q03,Q04: uc1.CATALOG[qid]['callable'] with uc1.CATALOG[qid]['parameters'] as the keyword order
dispatch.Q05,Q06,Q07: uc2.invoke_result_set(qid, {'parameters': ...}), which already resolves uc2.QUESTION_FUNCTIONS and uc2._PARAMETER_ORDER and converts Uc2InvocationError into a status triple

design.no_flat_concatenation: The four sources are exec'd into separate types.ModuleType namespaces rather than concatenated. uc1, uc2 and rotation each define warm_model, main, REPO_ROOT and _records, and uc1._records(df, columns) and uc2._records(df) do not take the same arguments, so flattening would silently keep whichever module came last.
design.package_aliasing: sys.modules['aviation_model'] and sys.modules['aviation_model.computed_schedule'] both point at the single exec'd ontology module. One Model per interpreter; a second one makes the free distinct(...) raise [Ambiguous model].
design.parameters: Read from EXPECTED_ANSWERS.yaml at generation time and emitted as Python literals, so the runner needs no manifest at run time. Default selection is the 25 manifest v1.2.0 enriched sets; INCLUDE_FROZEN / --all-parameter-sets adds the 24 frozen v1.1.1 sets including the deliberate parameter-error cases.
design.ordering: DISPLAY_ORDER = Q03, Q04, Q02, Q08, Q06, Q07, Q05, Q01, Q02F. Slowest last so output starts moving immediately.
design.failure_isolation: Every parameter set is wrapped; a failure is printed with a truncated traceback, recorded as FAILED in the summary, and the run continues.
design.warm_once: uc1.warm_model() is called once before the first question, reusing the existing retry through 'prepareIndex: model is currently locked'.

local.result: 25/25 enriched parameter sets returned, 1636 rows, 8.7 min wall clock including a 135.0s model sync
local.row_counts_vs_manifest: every one of the 25 matched the frozen expected_cardinality
local.second_run_final_bytes: Q04 only, 4/4 OK, confirms the file as delivered still executes after the entry-point and summary changes made since the full run

snowflake_side.how: The same file was staged to @PK_AVIATION_TEMPORAL.NOTEBOOKS.AVIATION_NOTEBOOK_STAGE/runner_smoke/ and imported by a two-cell throwaway notebook PK_AVIATION_TEMPORAL.NOTEBOOKS.RUNNER_SMOKE (SYSTEM$BASIC_RUNTIME, SYSTEM_COMPUTE_POOL_CPU, EXTERNAL_ACCESS_INTEGRATIONS = (PYPI_ACCESS)) executed headless with snow notebook execute. The notebook deliberately has no !pip cell so that the runner's own ensure_runtime() bootstrap is what is under test.
snowflake_side.result: PASS. snow notebook execute returned exit 0 in 14.6 minutes. The final cell is `failed = run_all_queries.run(); assert failed == 0`, so exit 0 means all 25 enriched parameter sets returned inside the Snowflake container. The runner's own ensure_runtime() supplied relationalai and protobuf there with no !pip cell; ConfigFromActiveSession supplied the credentials.
snowflake_side.control_experiment: A one-cell notebook with `failed = 3; assert failed == 0` was created, executed and dropped. It returned exit 1 with 'User app execution error ABORTED: AssertionError: 3 parameter set(s) failed', proving the exit code of the real run is load-bearing rather than vacuous.
snowflake_side.caveat: Headless execution does not persist cell output, so the printed tables from the Snowflake-side run are not retrievable; the assertion is the evidence. This is the SYSTEM$BASIC_RUNTIME notebook container, not the Workspaces notebook service, and the two ship different protobuf versions.

workspace.mechanism: snow sql PUT into the workspace URI, verified with LS. There is no `snow workspace` command in Snowflake CLI 3.16.0; the workspace filesystem is addressable over SQL and that is the repeatable route.
workspace.existing_user_file_untouched: aviation/queires/run_uc1_samples.py was read but not modified or overwritten.
workspace.why_not: Running a .py in Workspaces requires connecting a notebook service and pressing Run in the Snowsight UI. There is no CLI or SQL entry point for that, so it could not be driven from here.

workspaces_runtime_findings.compute: A .py in Workspaces runs on a Snowflake-managed notebook service, a container on an x86 SPCS compute pool whose ALLOWED_SPCS_WORKLOAD_TYPES include NOTEBOOK. Not a warehouse. SQL goes to a separate query warehouse.
workspaces_runtime_findings.cwd: The user's own aviation/queires/run_uc1_samples.py comments that the kernel CWD is the file's directory, not the workspace root. The runner does not depend on CWD at all.
workspaces_runtime_findings.packages: relationalai is PyPI-only and not in Snowflake's Anaconda channel. The notebook service needs either snowflake.snowpark.pypi_shared_repository (managed artifact repository, no egress required) or an external access integration with PyPI egress (this account has PYPI_ACCESS). Selecting an artifact repository disables integration-based installs, so it is one or the other. Package installs do not survive the weekend maintenance restart.
workspaces_runtime_findings.pip: No !pip magic in a .py file. subprocess [sys.executable, -m, pip, install, ...] is the route, and the user's existing workspace file proves it works there.
workspaces_runtime_findings.config: ConfigFromActiveSession is correct and needs no change; get_active_session() is documented for .py files in Workspaces and the ontology's _build_config() already branches on it.
workspaces_runtime_findings.protobuf: The legacy notebook problem (protobuf below 5.27, missing google.protobuf.runtime_version) is inverted in the Workspaces container runtime, which ships protobuf 6.x while lqp pins protobuf<6 with gencode built against 5.28. The runner probes `from google.protobuf import runtime_version` and `import lqp.proto.v1.logic_pb2` up front, then repairs in two escalating steps: TEMPORARILY_DISABLE_PROTOBUF_VERSION_CHECK, then a pinned protobuf into /tmp on the front of sys.path. Unverified in the Workspaces runtime specifically.

known_weaknesses: Not executed in Snowsight Workspaces itself. Running a .py there requires connecting a notebook service and pressing Run in the UI, and there is no CLI or SQL entry point for it. The Snowflake-side evidence is the SYSTEM$BASIC_RUNTIME notebook container, which ships a different protobuf, so the too-new-protobuf branch that matters for Workspaces is reasoned about rather than observed.
The Snowflake-side run took 14.6 minutes against 8.7 locally. That gap is container start plus a pip install plus a colder model sync, not a query regression, but it was not broken down.

The runner is 9,577 lines because it inlines the ontology and all three query modules. That is the cost of self-containment; it is generated, so it is not maintained by hand, but it is not pleasant to read in a Workspace editor.
Row counts are compared against the frozen manifest cardinality only. The row-by-row comparison stays in tests/; this is a runner, not an oracle.

The RelationalAI progress spinner writes carriage-return animation to stdout in a terminal. It renders as a wall of block characters in a redirected local log. In a notebook or Workspace runtime RAI switches to NotebookTaskProgress and this does not happen.
Wide result sets (Q05 has 19 columns, Q07 has 16) print as one long line each; display.width is deliberately unbounded so the table is not wrapped mid-row.

commands.deliver_to_workspace: snow sql -c rai --role RAI_DEMO_AVIATION_TEMPORAL -q "PUT 'file://$PWD/rai_code/manual/run_all_queries.py' 'snow://workspace/\"USER$piotr.kraus@relational.ai\".PUBLIC.\"DEFAULT$\"/versions/live/aviation/queires/' AUTO_COMPRESS=FALSE OVERWRITE=TRUE;"
